                                  16           This matter was initially randomly assigned to a magistrate judge who denied plaintiff’s

                                  17   application to proceed in forma pauperis, and required plaintiff to pay the filing fee by a specific

                                  18   date more than two weeks later. When plaintiff sought reconsideration (without complying with

                                  19   the rules applicable to such motions), the magistrate judge denied reconsideration on the merits,

                                  20   and extended the date to pay the filing fee to a date nearly two weeks beyond the entry of that

                                  21   order. After that deadline expired, and with no indication in the docket that plaintiff had filed the

                                  22   filing fee, the magistrate judge issued a report and recommendation suggesting the matter be

                                  23   dismissed on the basis that plaintiff had not established that he is indigent and had not paid the

                                  24   filing fee.

                                  25           Plaintiff’s payment of the filing fee was entered in the docket approximately two weeks

                                  26   later. In light of that payment, the recommendation for dismissal will not be adopted, and this

                                  27   matter may proceed in the ordinary course. That said, the complaint in this matter would have

                                  28   been subject to pre-filing review if it had been filed following the effective date of the pre-filing
                                          Case 3:26-cv-03425-RS              Document 16          Filed 06/24/26     Page 2 of 2




                                   1   review order in Firsov v. Scandinavian Airlines of North America, Inc., 3:25-cv-03691-EMC

                                   2   (N.D. Cal. June 23, 2026), Dkt. 113. There is little to suggest this action is any less frivolous than

                                   3   the plethora of prior cases described in that order. Plaintiff is advised that he may proceed only if

                                   4   he complies with the provisions of Rule 11 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, which states,

                                   5   in part:

                                   6                     By presenting to the court a pleading, written motion, or other
                                   7                     paper—whether by signing, filing, submitting, or later advocating
                                                         it—an attorney or unrepresented party certifies that to the best of the
                                   8                     person’s knowledge, information, and belief, formed after an inquiry
                                                         reasonable under the circumstances:
                                   9
                                                                 (1) it is not being presented for any improper purpose,
                                  10                             such as to harass, cause unnecessary delay, or
                                  11                             needlessly increase the cost of litigation;

                                  12                             (2) the claims, defenses, and other legal contentions
                                                                 are warranted by existing law or by a nonfrivolous
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13                             argument for extending, modifying, or reversing
                                                                 existing law or for establishing new law;
                                  14
                                                                 (3) the factual contentions have evidentiary support or,
                                  15                             if specifically so identified, will likely have evidentiary
                                                                 support after a reasonable opportunity for further
                                  16                             investigation or discovery . . . .
                                  17

                                  18              Although the pleadings of a pro se litigant are construed with liberality, plaintiff is
                                  19   cautioned that particularly in light of his overall litigation conduct, failure to comply with Rule 11
                                  20   in this action will expose him to the possibility of substantial monetary sanctions.
                                  21

                                  22   IT IS SO ORDERED.
                                  23

                                  24   Dated: June 24, 2026

                                  26                                                        RICHARD SEEBORG
                                                                                            Chief United States District Judge

                                  13          Plaintiff in this action is proceeding pro se. On April 24, 2026, the Court denied Plaintiff’s

                                  14   application to proceed in forma pauperis. Dkt. no. 6. Plaintiff brought a Motion for

                                  15   Reconsideration, which the Court denied on May 18, 2026. Dkt. No. 9.       In the May 18, 2026

                                  16   Order, the Court ordered that Plaintiff pay the filing fee no later than June 1, 2026. Id. He has

                                  17   not done so. Plaintiff also has not consented to the jurisdiction of a United States magistrate judge

                                  18   pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 636(c). Accordingly, this case shall be reassigned to a district judge with

                                  19   the recommendation that the case be dismissed without prejudice on the basis that Plaintiff has not

                                  20   established that he is indigent and has not paid the filing fee.

                                  21          If Plaintiff objects to this recommendation, he may file an objection within two weeks of

                                  22   the date on which he receives a copy of this Report & Recommendation.

                                  23          IT IS SO ORDERED.

                                  24

                                  25   Dated: June 2, 2026

                                  26                                                     ______________________________________
                                                                                         JOSEPH C. SPERO
                                  27                                                     United States Magistrate Judge

                                   1

                                   2

                                   5                                 NORTHERN DISTRICT OF CALIFORNIA

                                   6
                                         SERGEY FIRSOV,
                                   7                                                       Case No. 26-cv-03425-JCS
                                                        Plaintiff,
                                   8                                                       ORDER DENYING MOTION FOR
                                                 v.                                        RECONSIDERATION OF DENIAL OF
                                   9                                                       IN FORMA PAUPERIS APPLICATION
                                         WIZFAIR, LLC, et al.,                             AND EXTENDING DEADLINE TO
                                  10                                                       PAY FILING FEE TO JUNE 1, 2026
                                                        Defendants.
                                  11                                                       Dkt. no. 7

                                  12
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13

                                  14          Plaintiff has brought a motion for reconsideration of the Court’s denial of his in forma

                                  15   pauperis (“IFP”) application. As a preliminary matter, Plaintiff did not obtain leave of court to

                                  16   file a motion for reconsideration as required by Civil Local Rule 7-9, which requires that a party

                                  17   obtain leave of court prior to filing a motion for reconsideration. Notwithstanding this procedural

                                  18   error, the Court DENIES the motion for reconsideration. The hearing Plaintiff noticed for May

                                  19   27, 2026 is vacated.

                                  20          “[T]here is no formula set forth by statute, regulation, or case law to determine when

                                  21   someone is poor enough to earn IFP status.” Escobedo v. Applebees, 787 F.3d 1226, 1235 (9th Cir.

                                  22   2015). The undersigned, as well as “numerous other judges in this District across [a multitude of]

                                  23   other cases arising [predominantly] from Mr. Firsov’s air travel have [] denied his IFP applications

                                  24   when presented with similar financial information” to that presented in his affidavit. See L.F. by &

                                  25   Through Firsov v. Church of Scientology of Silicon Valley, 2025 WL 1616721, at *4 (N.D. Cal.

                                  26   June 5, 2025) (collecting nine other cases; based on the undersigned’s review, the total number of

                                  27   cases filed in this Court since 2025 is now over 20 – none granting IFP status). Most recently, just

                                  28   two months ago, Magistrate Judge Hixson found that even though Plaintiff reported a reduction of
                                           Case 3:26-cv-03425-RS           Document 9          Filed 05/18/26    Page 2 of 3




                                   1   his salary due to a “crisis in IT,” resulting in a gross monthly salary of $8,800 and a net monthly

                                   2   salary of $6,600, and despite claiming to be homeless, Plaintiff nonetheless did not qualify for IFP

                                   3   status. Firsov v. Frontier Airlines, Inc., 26-cv-1131 YGR, dkt. no. 8 (March 12, 2026 Report and

                                   4   Recommendation) at 4. (In that case, Plaintiff also claimed that he had monthly spousal and child

                                   5   support payments of $4,133.) Firsov v. Frontier Airlines, Inc., 26-cv-1131 YGR, dkt. no. 2 (IFP

                                   6   Application).

                                   7          Judge Hixson found that Plaintiff’s reduced salary and homeless status did not warrant

                                   8   reaching a different conclusion as to Plaintiff’s eligibility for IFP status from the one previously

                                   9   reached by a number of other judges of this Court, reasoning as follows:

                                  10                   First, while Plaintiff’s income has decreased, his income remains
                                                       substantial at $6,600 per month and, based on Plaintiff’s complaint,
                                  11                   he continues purchasing airline travel tickets (well after his reduction
                                                       in salary) and exercising discretionary spending at a level that belies
                                  12                   his inability to pay the filing fee for this action. See Compl. at 4-5;
Northern District of California




                                                       see also Firsov v. Skywest Airlines, No. 26-cv-0343-SVK, ECF No. 7
 United States District Court




                                  13                   at 2 finding Plaintiff had not shown that he could not afford to pay the
                                                       Court filing fee where he continued purchasing airline tickets, among
                                  14                   other discretionary spending.); Firsov v. Alaska Airlines, No. 25-cv-
                                                       2841-NW (NC), ECF No. 10 at 2 (finding Plaintiff had “not shown
                                  15                   that he could not afford to pay the Court filing fee if he adjusted or
                                                       deferred other of his discretionary expenses.”). Second, while
                                  16                   homelessness or inability to pay rent would point in favor of IFP
                                                       status, Plaintiff’s application is inconsistent on this matter: Despite
                                  17                   averring that he is homeless, he claims a monthly expense of $2,300
                                                       in rent owed. Compare ECF No. 2 at 3 with id. at 4.
                                  18
                                  19   Firsov v. Frontier Airlines, Inc., 26-cv-1131 YGR, dkt. no. 8 (March 12, 2026 Report and

                                  20   Recommendation) at 4-5. The undersigned agrees with Judge Hixson’s reasoning and conclusion.

                                  21          Likewise, the Court finds that Plaintiff has not established that he is unable to pay the

                                  22   filing fee in this case. First, Plaintiff states that his gross salary is now $10,920 a month, as

                                  23   compared to $8,800 just a few months ago, when Judge Hixson found that Plaintiff was not

                                  24   eligible for IFP status. Furthermore, Plaintiff’s statement, without explanation that his net salary

                                  25   is only $4,200 – that is, that his take-home pay is less than half than his salary – is not credible.

                                  26   The Court notes that in an IFP application filed approximately one year ago, Plaintiff listed a gross

                                  27   salary (for the same job he has listed on all of his IFP applications) of $11,000/month (just $8 a

                                  28   month more than he lists in this case) and yet listed a net salary of $8,000/month. See Firsov v.
                                                                                          2
                                           Case 3:26-cv-03425-RS           Document 9              Filed 05/18/26   Page 3 of 3




                                   1   Scandinavian Airlines, 25-cv-3691 EMC, dkt. no. 2. While Plaintiff now claims to owe

                                   2   $4,500/month in spousal and child support payments (as compared to $4,133/month in the case

                                   3   discussed above), the increase as to these obligations is more than offset by the increase in

                                   4   Plaintiff’s salary.

                                   5           Second, the allegations in this case (and in the many other cases Plaintiff has filed in this

                                   6   Court) reflect that he continues to engage in expensive international travel, including hotels and

                                   7   even charges for transporting a dog. See dkt. no. 1. In light of Plaintiff’s expenditures and

                                   8   resources, the undersigned agrees with every other judge of this Court to have addressed the

                                   9   question, that Plaintiff has not shown that he cannot afford to pay the Court filing fee if he adjusts

                                  10   or defers other discretionary expenses.

                                  11           Plaintiff’s deadline to pay the full filing fee is extended to June 1, 2026. Failure to pay

                                  12   the filing fee may result in dismissal of this case.
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13           IT IS SO ORDERED.

                                  14   Dated: May 18, 2026

                                  15                                                     ______________________________________
                                                                                         JOSEPH C. SPERO
                                  16                                                     United States Magistrate Judge
